recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-39132 unless a future work group decision changes CodeableReference profiling policy.
issue_request: FHIR-39132 was a Published FHIR-core R5 change request resolved Persuasive. It asked to clarify the CodeableReference narrative sentence "If they are specified on both" so readers would not construe "both" as meaning only the .reference and .concept child elements.
initial_application: Git commit af5f22e7cfac05593b3bd86d61c2a3cc21a53734 explicitly applied FHIR-39132 on 2023-02-14 by changing source/references.html to the proposed wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini makes CodeableReference an active datatype and maps codeablereference to the references page. Later same-paragraph work for FHIR-39176 aligned the narrative with sdf-24 and sdf-25 by using SHALL NOT, and FHIR-38957 clarified the targetProfile/binding mapping while preserving the child-element prohibition.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active source now states directly that targetProfile and binding constraints declared on CodeableReference apply to CodeableReference.reference and CodeableReference.concept respectively and SHALL NOT be specified directly on .reference or .concept. The old proposed sentence remains only in an HTML comment.
